questions.q: What gap does AWS Lake Formation close that plain IAM and S3 policies don't cover on their own?
options: Fine-grained, table- and column-level access control — neither IAM nor S3 policies natively understand individual table columns
Lake Formation replaces IAM entirely and is not layered on top of it
It encrypts data at rest, which IAM cannot do
It is only used for billing, not access control
questions.explain: Lake Formation sits on top of IAM and the Glue Data Catalog specifically to add database-, table-, and column-level permissions that plain IAM/S3 policies don't natively express.

questions.q: What is the 'named resource method' of granting Lake Formation permissions?
options: Granting permissions by selecting specific databases or tables directly, as opposed to granting against an LF-Tag expression
A method that only works through the AWS CLI, never the console
Granting permissions to IAM user names instead of roles
A deprecated method no longer available in the console
questions.explain: The named resource method is the direct approach: pick specific databases/tables by name. LF-Tags are the alternative, scaling via tag-based grants instead.

questions.q: In the Table and column permissions screen, what does checking a permission under 'Grantable permissions' actually do?
options: Lets the recipient re-grant that permission to someone else, separate from being able to use it themselves
Automatically applies the permission to every table in the database
Grants Super permission regardless of what else is checked
Removes the permission from Table permissions
questions.explain: Grantable permissions is Lake Formation's grant-option equivalent — it controls whether the recipient can pass the permission along to others.

questions.q: When would you use Advanced cell-level filters instead of Simple column-based access?
options: When you need to restrict both specific columns AND specific rows together, not just a list of included/excluded columns
When you only need to restrict columns, never rows
They are identical options with different names
Only when granting Insert, never Select
questions.explain: Simple column-based access only restricts columns. Advanced cell-level filters apply a named data filter that can combine column and row restrictions together.

questions.q: What does the Lake Formation GRANT statement 'GRANT SELECT, DESCRIBE ON TABLE retail.inventory TO ROLE AnalyticsReadOnlyRole;' correspond to in the console?
options: The same thing the three-section Grant permissions wizard collects: the resource, the permissions, and the principal
A bucket policy JSON document
An ACL entry on the underlying S3 objects
An Azure RBAC role assignment
questions.explain: The console wizard's resource picker, permissions checkboxes, and principal selection together produce exactly this kind of grant, whether issued as this statement or via the CLI.
